newsitem.title: USA: U.S. T-bond futures rise after auction, end higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. T-bond futures rise after auction, end higher.

text.p: A well-received auction of 30-year U.S. Treasury debt sparked a rally that hoisted U.S. Treasury bond futures well into the plus column.

After languishing modestly lower much of the session, T-bond futures began rising as the market discerned that the 30-year bond had fetched relatively better demand than the week's earlier two auctions and certainly stronger results than many had expected for the long bond.
The bond produced an average yield of 6.619 percent, with a one-basis-point tail. Forecasts had ranged from about 6.64 percent to slightly above 6.62 percent for average yield.
The bid-cover ratio was a strong 2.68, which analysts said eclipsed non-competitive bids that only totalled $258 million.

"Actually, it was a really nice response," said Jim Collins, senior vice president, Smith Barney, of the bond market's ensuing rally. "You could really lay it all at the feet of the auction...I think people liked the bid/cover."
Although the non-comp bids were roughly $100 million lower than the long-term average for the three-year auction, "people didn't seem to mind very much," he said.
The rise occurred as shorts capitulated, then turned buyers, which tugged nearby T-bond futures above resistance.

Although the auction results listed foreign institutional participation at zero, floor brokers noted unconfirmed talk that overseas firms may have bought through a large West Coast fund manager, which they said took a big portion of the sale.

December T-bond futures hesitated at 113-24/32, then poked through key resistance at 114-00 on local and then dealer shortcovering. It set off buystops there as dealers switched positions and turned buyers, though flows stayed on both ways.
The ability of nearby T-bond futures to shake off the morning's dollar-related losses and rally to close above resistance could portend more gains, some brokers said.
"Closing above 114-08/32 is significant," said a floor broker in T-bond futures. "If we hold these gains and build a platform, we could see 115-00 early next week."
T-bond futures slid overnight and in early pit trading after the U.S. dollar skidded against the yen.

The yen rallied when Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of the Ministry of Finance's International Finance Bureau, was quoted in a Japanese financial newspaper on Thursday as saying that the dollar's correction of last year's sharp slide against the yen was about done.
But T-bonds bounced off 112-29/32 and grinded upward.

December T-bonds settled up 21/32 at 114-09/32, muni-bonds rose 17/32 to 116-25/32, 10-year notes added 8/32 to 110-08/32, March T-bills ended flat at 94.96, and Eurodollars also ended unchanged, at 94.46. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
